- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for days 1–7.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., bullish → bearish → bullish), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
